For 0 ≤ σ < 1, r is not O(ε); for σ = 0 it does not shrink at all. The contribution therefore overstates the accuracy established for the full parameter range.

issues.failure_explanation: When σ > 0 and x^0 is stationary, the KL level set can be empty, so the prescribed initial value gap gives no distance bound. For example, take p=0, q=δ_[0,2], f(x,y)=−0.01(1−cos(πy)), and c≡−1 with a positive smoothness bound small enough that the lifted constraint is inactive. Then Ψ≡0, so the KL assumption is vacuous for σ=1, C=γ=1 and θ=1/2. With ε=0.1 and y^0=1, the initial gap is 0.02≤0.05. Both algorithms leave y=1 unchanged because its inner gradient is zero. Yet Y*(x)={0,2}, so its distance is 1, whereas the promised bound is at most 2√0.05<1 at every iteration.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate the initial-success case: if x^0 is already (ε,r)-stationary, retain only the prescribed initial value-gap guarantee. Assert the additional inner-distance bound for a first successful iterate reached from a non-(ε,r)-stationary initial point, or impose that distance accuracy explicitly on the initial pair.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted existence of a pair satisfying both outer stationarity and the stated inner-distance bound is false for permitted initial inputs.
issues.title: The inner-distance guarantee fails when the initial outer point is already stationary
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the initial-case output contract preserves the outer stationarity result and its rate, but the stated inner guarantee cannot be retained for all existing inputs.

issues.failure_explanation: A proper closed convex p need not have a nonempty subdifferential at every domain point. For example, p(t)=−√t+δ_[0,1](t) has empty subdifferential at 0. With f independent of x, the outer residual there is infinite. For σ>0, K_x is then infinite, outside the finite positive-radius hypotheses of the error-bound lemma as stated. The claimed all-x proof does not establish finiteness of this input.

The proof already establishes the necessary slope bound on every lower positive level, so this finite K satisfies the error-bound lemma without any finiteness assumption on the outer residual.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed growth argument has an uncovered allowed case at points with empty outer subdifferentials, which are included in the claimed domains of the downstream growth and Hölder results.
